nodes.title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents
nodes.abstract: AI coding agents operate in iterative loops: they modify code, run tools, inspect the results, and decide what to do next. nodes.title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs
nodes.abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting enables reasoning in large language models but produces explanations that are difficult to verify, expensive to generate, and not always faithful. nodes.title: scHFBiMamba: a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder for cardiac disease-state classification from single-nucleus RNA-seq data
nodes.abstract: To evaluate whether a compact bidirectional state-space autoencoder improves joint classification of species, cell type, and disease state from single-nucleus RNA-sequencing profiles in heart failure (HF), while yielding interpretable gene attributions. nodes.abstract: Foundation models need to support diverse inference budgets, yet training a separate model for each budget duplicates pretraining effort. nodes.title: RIECNN: Real-Time Image Enhanced CNN for Traffic Sign Recognition
nodes.abstract: Traffic sign recognition plays a crucial role in the development of autonomous cars to reduce the accident rate and promote road safety. nodes.abstract: Modern AI systems increasingly combine large language models (LLMs) with human experts, using the LLM to handle routine queries while deferring uncertain cases for expert review. nodes.title: GesBench: When and Where Do Multimodal Language Models Perceive Social Meaning?
nodes.abstract: Human social perception is incremental: we infer intent before an utterance is complete, revise our interpretation as new cues arrive, and attend to specific facial, gestural, or prosodic signals that shape social meaning. nodes.title: UDHRBench: Benchmarking Human Rights in Large Language Models
nodes.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed in contexts requiring adherence to ethical and legal norms, yet their alignment with internationally recognized human rights standards remains underexplored. nodes.title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals
nodes.abstract: Batch risk-based inspection scheduling struggles to detect a critical failure class: food facilities with recent clean inspections that subsequently develop severe violations. nodes.title: SocraticRepair: Planning-Guided Socratic Tutoring for Program Debugging and Misconception Repair
nodes.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in computer science education. nodes.title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces

nodes.title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
nodes.abstract: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. nodes.title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments
nodes.abstract: Words are increasingly becoming an interface for action: large language models (LLMs) can now invoke tools, operate devices, and make decisions that affect the physical world. Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning, we train Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora built from the same 1,625 real-world usage scenarios. The corpora differ only in the predominant motive they attribute to users of AI chatbots: helping ...

nodes.title: SarcasTraps: Effect of Sarcasm on Turkish Hate Speech Detection
nodes.abstract: Standard hate speech detection datasets often emphasize explicit harmful language, but directed harm can also be expressed indirectly, without clearly hateful wording. Sarcasm is one such form of indirect expression, as it can convey harmful intent through mock praise, exaggeration, humor, or apparent politeness. In this paper, we introduce SarcasTraps, a targeted external test set for analyzing the effect of sarcasm...
nodes.delta: [Judge & Detection • 28th Percentile Divergence] These findings show that both fine-tuned hate speech detectors and zero-shot LLMs struggle when sarcasm is involved, and SarcasTraps provides quantitative evidence of this challenge through a targeted Turkish test set.

nodes.title: Proactive Physical AI through Continuous Observation and Timely Intervention
nodes.abstract: Physical AI is commonly formulated around an explicitly specified task: given a goal or instruction, a system perceives, reasons, and acts. In many real-world settings, however, important tasks emerge from continuously changing world states before a person explicitly formulates them. nodes.title: MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine
nodes.abstract: Drug discovery remains a resource-intensive and time-consuming process, involving billions of dollars and a decade of development to advance a drug to market. While many in silico tools have accelerated this process, operating them still demands substantial time, effort, and expertise from medicinal chemists. nodes.title: The Value of Being Wrong: Self-Mined Visual In-Context Learning from Errors
nodes.abstract: Visual in-context learning (ICL) enables vision-language models (VLMs) to adapt at test time via demonstration examples, but its effectiveness depends critically on the examples selected. nodes.title: WeGR: Towards Unified Generative Retrieval via Behavior-aware Tokenization and Preference Alignment
nodes.abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) offers a promising paradigm for industrial search by unifying candidate generation within an autoregressive framework. nodes.delta: [Token & Knowledge • 22th Percentile Divergence] Moreover, a six-week online A/B test on a large-scale e-commerce search platform achieves relative gains of 2.539% in orders, 1.508% in CTR, and 1.381% in CVR, while reducing CPU and GPU usage by 25.5% and 26.1%.

nodes.title: PRAISE: A Reproducible Workflow for Non-Programmer Scientists to Implement Published AI Models
nodes.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are increasingly developed, published and used across scientific fields. Researchers, students and industry professionals who want to apply these models to their own research questions often lack the programming and data science expertise to do so. nodes.title: From Suboptimal to Optimal: One-Step Latent Flow Policies for Offline Reinforcement Learning
nodes.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning aims to learn effective policies from fixed datasets without environment interaction. nodes.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models show strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving by leveraging world knowledge and understanding to excel in long-tail scenarios. nodes.title: TabGift: A Context-Efficient Foundation Model for Tabular Data Generation
nodes.abstract: Tabular data generation aims to synthesize realistic samples from limited observations while faithfully capturing the underlying data distribution. nodes.title: Glasseek: A Transparent Recipe for Training and Trustworthy Evaluation of DeepSearch Agents
nodes.abstract: Deep search enables language agents to solve complex information-seeking tasks through iterative web exploration. nodes.title: Governing Copyright Responsibly in the Era of Generative AI
nodes.abstract: Large language models are trained on collections that may include scholarly works, while authors generally lack work-level information about whether and how their works were used. nodes.title: MAGNET: Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network for Connectome Generation
nodes.abstract: Functional brain connectome represents neural connectivity as a matrix of pairwise interactions between brain regions. Generation of functional connectomes is not only a question of validity; rather, having satisfied the constraints on the correlation matrix, the next step is to recover the class-conditional geometry buried under coarse labels. nodes.title: ProbabilityBench: Model Evaluation and Calibration with Exact Ground-Truth Uncertainty
nodes.abstract: Evaluating model uncertainty on real-world data is challenging because each instance provides only a single observed label, leaving true conditional class probabilities unknown. nodes.title: Understanding Personalization Gains in Whisper ASR
nodes.abstract: Whisper-style ASR models provide strong zero-shot transcription, but their residual errors are not evenly distributed across datasets, recording conditions, and metadata-based groups. nodes.title: CWE-bench: Refocusing Agentic Security from Exploitation to Defense
nodes.abstract: Cybersecurity evaluations of AI agents have focused largely on offense, yet a working exploit does not show that an agent can make software safe. An attacker needs to exploit only one vulnerability; a defender must find and fix all of them. nodes.abstract: Detecting credit card fraud is notoriously difficult because fraudulent charges make up less than 0.2% of total transactions. nodes.title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion
nodes.abstract: Neural operator splitting composes a library of neural operators, one per physical mechanism, into zero-shot simulators of new equations. nodes.title: Neos: Learning to Interleave Search and Visual Reasoning
nodes.abstract: Recent multimodal deep search agents have advanced tool use and visual content retrieval, yet they still struggle to convert intermediate visual evidence into actionable guidance for subsequent search, limiting their effectiveness in long-horizon settings. nodes.title: VL-DocIR: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Long Document Information Retrieval
nodes.abstract: Vision-based document retrieval has improved rapidly, but current evaluation settings still emphasize short documents and single relevant pages. nodes.title: PatientWM: Towards Generalizable Clinical World Models via Unified Patient States
nodes.abstract: Clinical decisions depend on anticipating how a patient's condition will evolve as treatment is adjusted and new evidence becomes available. nodes.title: Gradient Routing Localizes and Removes Unintended Behaviors in RL
nodes.abstract: We propose a mitigation to reward hacking in reinforcement learning. nodes.title: Superintelligence and the Triple Risk of an AI Race
nodes.abstract: On many estimates, artificial general intelligence (AGI) is likely to emerge within the next few decades or even sooner. nodes.abstract: AI-assisted research leaves instructions, computations, artifact revisions and checks whose relationships matter when another researcher receives the work. nodes.abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models (FD-SLMs) support simultaneous listening and speaking, but often lag behind half-duplex spoken language models (HD-SLMs) in general capabilities. nodes.title: Force-Modulated Dexterity: Unified Compliance for Contact-Rich Manipulation

nodes.title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors
